expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: "No. The check cannot fire in the incident it was written for."

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: "TOCTOU. Redelivery is often concurrent with attempt 1 still in flight. Both read 'no charge,' both proceed."

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: "Idempotency key on every Stripe call, derived deterministically from the message/order ID"

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Explicitly labels three categories: Defect (charged twice), Mistake (retry called charge again), Hazard (path not idempotent)

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: "The hazard isn't in the worker — it's that your queue is at-least-once and side-effecting consumers aren't idempotent"

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: "Every other consumer of that queue has this bug latent: refunds, transfers, provisioning, emails, webhook fanout"

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: "The 'second time' is the real finding" followed by Control-rung device recommendations

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: All causality framed as system properties (queue semantics, idempotency), no personal attribution
